scope: 29 current PROVIDER_CATALOG entries plus PayPal as an adjacent directory candidate
method: Public vendor documentation and vendor-owned repositories. Directory metadata is corroborating inventory evidence, not proof that our client can authenticate. No account authentication, client registration, tool calls, or external writes performed.
compatibility_baseline: The app's built-in hosted-MCP sign-in currently targets public OAuth clients with Dynamic Client Registration (DCR). Static OAuth credentials, confidential clients, bearer tokens, local processes, and partner allowlists must be evaluated separately. A documented public-DCR path makes a provider a validation candidate, not a certified migration.
parity_policy: These are documented capability differences and migration constraints, not an exhaustive REST-vs-MCP diff. Unverified parity is not a reason by itself to reject a migration. Preserve existing public action names and all toolkit scopes, and validate actual workflows before retiring a native adapter.

Current Drive MCP reference does not list move, delete, or permission-mutation tools.
Current app has Calendar, Gmail, Drive, Docs and Sheets toolkits. Replacing only the three directory entries loses two scopes.
Docs/Sheets create workflows may require Drive create_file. Their tool references use /mcp while general setup examples may use versioned URLs, so verify the exact endpoint during integration.
